diagnosis.root_cause: The OLT health record is stale and falsely reports all 8 PONs failed. Its run_date is 2025-11-11, while current probes show the OLT responding to ping and SNMP, all tested ONUs online, 207 of 214 ONUs online, normal OLT resources, and active customer traffic.
evidence: The OLT answers ping, SNMP, and the requested OID subtree, so this is not an OLT failure.
OLT CPU, memory, temperature, and uptime are within healthy ranges.
The subscriber ONU is online with normal RX power of about -19.7 dBm and TX power of about +2.4 dBm.
All seven visible peers on EPON0/5 are online with normal optical readings, and the live PON probe confirms all seven respond online.
The OLT population has 207 of 214 ONUs online, which is consistent with normal background offline levels rather than an OLT-wide outage.
Customer traffic is active and the router heartbeat is healthy.
The expected customer VLAN 1035 is present and correct, and RADIUS state is consistent.
The alarm claims all PONs failed, but live evidence shows the PON and OLT are operating; therefore the alarm is a false critical generated by the health check.
The stored health record is stale by far more than a few days, so its all-PON failure result describes historical or invalid monitoring state rather than the current network.

remediation.action: Discard the stale health result, run a fresh OLT/PON health check, and clear the critical alarm after validation. Fix the monitoring pipeline to enforce record freshness, prevent stale failure lists from driving overall_status, and reconcile summary status with live PON and ONU detail. No field repair or customer-side intervention is indicated.

ground_truth.root_cause: The stored health record carries a run_date of 2025-11-11, ten months before the current date. The health check has not run since. The OLT has 58 days of uptime, answers every probe normally and is serving all its customers; the alarm describes a condition that no longer exists, if it ever did.
expected_reasoning: The health record reports critical with all eight PONs failed
Its run_date is 2025-11-11, ten months before the scenario's capture time
A stored record that old describes history, not current state
The live probe answers normally: the ONU is online with RX -19.71 and TX 2.42
OLT ping and SNMP succeed, oid_subtree_responds is true and uptime is 58 days
58 days of uptime postdates the stored record, so the device has restarted since it was written
CPU 24, memory 18 and temperature 42 are all at healthy baseline
Customers are authenticated with normal sessions and seven days of steady traffic
The finding is not an outage but that OLT health monitoring has not run for ten months

expected_escalation.review_reason: OLT health checks have not run since 2025-11-11; the schedule is not active

distractors: The alarm text is identical to a genuine critical
The record is internally consistent and only its date betrays it
Nothing in the alarm payload signals that it is stale
